12 October 2026 · Pocket Flight · Local aircraft rebuild

Finch U–2 cockpit rebuilt

The entire cockpit subtree has been replaced in the runtime aircraft asset. The preserved airframe supplies the wing, body, tail, engine and landing-gear geometry. The new cabin uses a lower panel and glare shield, contoured bucket seats, compact avionics, native dual control sticks, adjustable pedal geometry and a complete rear-hinged canopy.

Open private testerEditable Blender modelRuntime GLBRebuild source

Canopy fitted to the fuselage

The separate round sill rails left exposed capped ends over the nose. They have been removed. A continuous porcelain surround now closes around the glazing and seats against the actual fuselage mesh, with a recessed seal and a thin internal windshield header. The extra free-ended cabin reinforcement rods have also been removed.

Design decisions

The handbook’s sections 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 16.1–16.2 require coherent structure, equipment packaging, pilot clearance and real articulated pivots. The new assembly replaces the old bulky dashboard and generic cockpit additions rather than adding more decorative rods. The canopy moves with its glazing, rails, rear bow and latch handles. Its hinge, clevises and gas-support mounting points are authored in the model and exported as datums.

Diamond’s DA20 cockpit and manufacturer brochure informed the trainer layout: outward visibility, bucket seats, dual stick controls and restrained instrument packaging. Finch remains an original concept aircraft.

The model checks both signs of pitch and roll at 18 stick poses against the seats, panel, coaming and console. It checks glazing at 12 canopy angles from 0° to 55° against furniture and the fuselage. The outer glazing boundary cell is excluded from the latter test because it contains the intended bonded sill/header contact. All sampled intersection counts are zero.

Verification

  • 113 repository tests passed, 47,257 assertions. Runtime tests include 72 mechanism poses, support endpoints, exported pilot-eye roof clearance, fixed furniture and neutral reset.
  • Private tester and game TypeScript/production builds passed.
  • 7 dedicated cockpit browser checks passed with zero browser/shader errors. The rebuilt geometry retains all 122 full-span airflow paths.
  • The saved Blender file reopened independently: 275 editable meshes, 134,989 triangles, zero nonfinite vertices, a continuous mounted surround and the expected hinge datum.

The cockpit is an original concept model. Head clearance uses a simple seated-pilot envelope, not a complete anthropometric study. The avionics graphics are illustrative. Private mechanical mode demonstrates controls and access motion; aerodynamic readouts retain the neutral main-wing reference. The shared runtime asset updates Finch’s appearance in the game as well.

Repeatable workflow

bun run finch:cockpit
bun test tests/aircraft-mechanics.test.ts tests/finch-geometry.test.ts
bun run lab:build
bun run lab:cockpit-check

The build uses the preserved local assets/finch/Finch-U2-base.blend. It saves the editable cabin before batching the exported static parts. The original runtime asset and previous cockpit screenshot are preserved under output/finch-cockpit-before/.
